title: PLEASE HELP! Core Script update ruined my game :(

posts.author: GreenInvader
posts.body:
I have been working on the same project for years (literally over 3000 hours), since RPG MV days and
eventually imported my project to RPG MZ two years ago.
I have never had any issues with all of the mv plugins I was using because I'm assuming it was running on the MV engine or some sort of hybrid. Today I accidentally updated the Core Script
in an attempt to get the Battle Test to work
and now my game will not start at all. I can open the project and edit things, but the actual game test will not work. I can't bring up the console in order to see what the exact issue might be either.
From experience and research, I'm assuming
an incompatibility with the plugins is the cause, now that I'm actually using the MZ engine...
Is there any way to revert my MZ core script back to the way it was
in it's "unknown" form from MV? I am really trying to avoid having to redo all my plugin work from over the years
as it's very specific and I'm not sure there are replacements for much of it

I also opened up a back up of the project from before the update and it was now at 1.0, instead of "unknown". So to clarify, the file I'm looking to copy from a new MV project to MZ is rpg_core.js ?
I sincerely appreciate the help!

posts.author: caethyril
posts.body:
I think you've done something wrong, since that function definitely exists in the core scripts of both MV and MZ.
This announcement has precise instructions for updating an RMMV project's core script version, under
Updating your Projects
:
Announcement - RPG Maker MV - v1.6.1 Stable Release!
6/21/2018 Everyone, please read the instructions carefully. The bugs that are being reported shouldn't happen if the correct files were even copied properly. Such examples like the "CTRL BUG" shouldn't happen if you copied index.html, package.json, the rpg*.js files and so on.  I also received...
forums.rpgmakerweb.com
Note that the first step is to make a copy as a backup in case something goes wrong. This is good advice in general.

posts.author: Nowis-337
posts.body:
In your project folder ---> js folder

posts.author: caethyril
posts.body:
Here's the relevant part from the thread I linked in my previous post:
Archeia said:
Create a new project or go to the NewData folder in your RPG Maker MV root (where MV is installed) folder. Copy the following items and replace the ones in your existing project:
Copy the file "index.html" and "package.json" from NewData to your project
Copy the files libs folder, "rpg_*.js" (example: rpg_core) files from NewData/js to your project js folder
Do not replace your plugins.js !
Done!
Click to expand...
In your case you can source the files from your working backup instead of NewData.

..."fear monger"? I was giving a personal tip from experience to OP.
As your source states, HDDs have a shorter life span, and that's a fact. You can rely on it, but SSDs or Cloud Services are a safer option.
Mechanical drives can deteriorate and the magnetic surface may create bad sectors. SSDs can also lose charge, but it is still more durable.
SSDs also don't have moving parts like actuator arms and spinning platters.
